identity.name: Linux Host File Mass-Encryption for Impact — SAFE-MODE (T1486 / T1490)
identity.summary: A Linux ransomware-style payload rewrites a seeded victim directory with a ransomware extension and drops a ransom note (SAFE-MODE writes an inert marker, no real crypto), then inhibits recovery by deleting snapshots/backups. Cortex XDR for Linux fires mass-rewrite, ransom-note, and recovery-inhibition BIOCs into one Impact incident — a Linux-host variant distinct from the ESXi card.
identity.description: Linux is now a first-class ransomware target: Akira, Black Basta, and RansomEXX affiliates ship dedicated ELF encryptors that walk a victim's filesystem, encrypt files in place, append a ransomware extension, and drop a ransom note in every traversed directory — the canonical Data Encrypted for Impact (T1486) behaviour — and then inhibit recovery (T1490) by removing local snapshots, backups, and shadow copies. This card reproduces that telemetry shape on a single Linux host (NOT an ESXi hypervisor — that is the distinct TTP-2026-0006 / SIM-EDR-007), giving the EDR plane a second, independent detection variant for T1486 so a DC can prove the rule fires on host-level encryption as well as hypervisor-level. SAFE-MODE: the payload seeds an isolated victim directory, then for each file appends the `.cortexlock` ransomware extension and overwrites the content with an inert `CORTEXSIM-SAFE-MODE-NOT-ENCRYPTED` marker (no real cryptography, fully reversible by cleanup), and drops a `READ_ME_CORTEXSIM.txt` note; the recovery-inhibition step deletes only CortexSim-created snapshot/backup artefacts. The detection model is behavioural and content-based: (1) a rapid mass file-rewrite/rename BIOC fires when one process modifies an abnormal number of files with a new uniform extension in a short window — the encryptor fingerprint; (2) a ransom-note BIOC fires on the recurring note filename written across many directories; (3) a recovery-inhibition BIOC fires on snapshot/backup deletion commands; (4) validation XQL confirms each in xdr_data. IOC signatures pin the ransomware extension and the ransom-note filename. A correlation rule fuses the mass-encryption, ransom-note, and recovery-inhibition signals from one host into a single critical Impact incident.

execution.framework_reference_id: T1486 — Linux host file mass-encryption (SAFE-MODE marker overwrite) + T1490 recovery inhibition

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR Linux agent installed and reporting healthy on the target host.
prerequisites.check_command: systemctl is-active cortex-agent || ps aux | grep -i traps

prerequisites.description: Isolated lab host — the payload only touches the seeded /tmp/cortexsim_victim directory and CortexSim-created snapshot artefacts (lab only).

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE Linux ransomware telemetry — NO real encryption, fully reversible.
# step-1: seed an isolated victim directory and discover files (T1083)
VDIR=/tmp/cortexsim_victim; mkdir -p $VDIR; for i in $(seq 1 40); do echo "original content $i" > $VDIR/document_$i.dat; done
find $VDIR -type f | head -1000 > /tmp/cortexsim_targetlist.txt
# step-2: mass rewrite + ransomware extension + SAFE-MODE inert marker (T1486)
while read -r f; do printf 'CORTEXSIM-SAFE-MODE-NOT-ENCRYPTED' > "${f}.cortexlock" && rm -f "$f"; done < /tmp/cortexsim_targetlist.txt
# step-3: drop a ransom note in the victim directory (T1486)
printf 'Your files are locked (CORTEXSIM SAFE-MODE — nothing was actually encrypted).' > $VDIR/READ_ME_CORTEXSIM.txt
# step-4: inhibit recovery — delete ONLY CortexSim snapshot/backup artefacts (T1490)
rm -f /tmp/cortexsim_snapshot_*.img /tmp/cortexsim_backup_*.tar 2>/dev/null; echo '[*] recovery-inhibition step issued (CortexSim artefacts only)'

expected_artifacts.description: Many files rewritten with a uniform ransomware extension by one process in a short window.
Ransom-note file written into the victim directory.

cleanup.code:
VDIR=/tmp/cortexsim_victim
for f in $VDIR/*.cortexlock; do orig="${f%.cortexlock}"; [ -e "$f" ] && echo 'restored content' > "$orig" && rm -f "$f"; done 2>/dev/null
rm -f $VDIR/READ_ME_CORTEXSIM.txt /tmp/cortexsim_targetlist.txt
rm -rf $VDIR
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-EDR-008 cleanup complete — SAFE-MODE markers removed, victim dir restored'

iocs.context: Uniform ransomware extension appended to mass-rewritten files — Linux-host encryptor signature (SAFE-MODE marker stands in for the real extension).
Ransom note dropped across encrypted directories — recurring-note ransomware signature.

biocs.name: EDR-008 Rapid Mass File Rewrite With Uniform New Extension
biocs.description: A single process modifies/creates an abnormally large number of files carrying one new uniform extension in a short window — the host-level file-encryption fingerprint (T1486). Distinct from the ESXi VMDK-adjacent mass-write BIOC on TTP-2026-0006.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE, ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_RENAME)
| filter action_file_extension in ("cortexlock", "akira", "locked", "crypt", "encrypted")
| bin _time span=1m
| comp count() as files_rewritten by actor_process_instance_id, actor_process_image_name, agent_hostname, _time
| filter files_rewritten >= 20
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, files_rewritten

biocs.name: EDR-008 Ransom Note Written Across Multiple Directories
biocs.description: A recurring ransom-note filename is written into multiple directories by one process — the note-drop stage of a ransomware encryptor (T1486).
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_name contains_any ("READ_ME", "RANSOM", "_DECRYPT_", "HOW_TO_RESTORE", "akira_readme")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_directory) as note_dirs by actor_process_instance_id, agent_hostname
| filter note_dirs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_instance_id, note_dirs

biocs.name: EDR-008 Local Recovery Inhibition — Snapshot Or Backup Deletion
biocs.description: Deletion of local snapshots/backups/shadow copies on a Linux host — recovery inhibition (T1490) co-occurring with mass file rewriting.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("rm", "lvremove", "btrfs", "zfs", "rsnapshot", "shred")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("snapshot", "backup", ".img", ".tar", "--delete", "destroy")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: EDR-008 Validate Mass File Rewrite With Ransomware Extension
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_extension in ("cortexlock", "akira", "locked", "crypt", "encrypted")
| comp count() as files_rewritten by actor_process_image_name, agent_hostname
| filter files_rewritten >= 20
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, files_rewritten

xql_queries.name: EDR-008 Validate Ransom Note Creation
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_name contains_any ("READ_ME", "RANSOM", "_DECRYPT_", "HOW_TO_RESTORE")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, action_file_name, action_file_directory

xql_queries.name: EDR-008 Validate Local Recovery Inhibition
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("rm", "lvremove", "btrfs", "zfs", "shred")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("snapshot", "backup", ".img", ".tar")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: EDR-008 Hunt Encryptor Process Lineage Across Hosts
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_extension in ("cortexlock", "akira", "locked", "crypt")
| comp count() as encrypted_files, count_distinct(agent_hostname) as hosts by causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_image_name
| sort desc encrypted_files
| fields causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_image_name, encrypted_files, hosts

correlation_rules.name: Ransomware — Linux Host Mass-Encryption + Recovery Inhibition (Same Host)
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(EDR-008 Rapid Mass File Rewrite With Uniform New Extension) AND (BIOC(EDR-008 Ransom Note Written Across Multiple Directories) OR BIOC(EDR-008 Local Recovery Inhibition — Snapshot Or Backup Deletion)) — fuses the encryption, ransom-note, and recovery-inhibition stages from one host into a single critical Impact incident.

use_cases.name: Ransomware Impact Detection — Linux Host File Encryption
use_cases.description: Detect and stitch a Linux-host file mass-encryption + recovery-inhibition chain (a second, host-level detection variant of T1486 distinct from the ESXi card).

test_cases.objective: Mass file-rewrite, ransom-note, and recovery-inhibition each fire their Cortex XDR BIOC.
preconditions: Cortex XDR Linux agent >= 8.4.0 installed and healthy.
BIOCs from this card imported and enabled.
steps: Run SIM-EDR-008 steps 1-4 against the seeded victim directory.
Observe the per-stage BIOC alerts in the Cortex console.
success_criteria: BIOC `EDR-008 Rapid Mass File Rewrite With Uniform New Extension` fires within 60s with files_rewritten >= 20.
BIOC `EDR-008 Ransom Note Written Across Multiple Directories` fires on the note drop.
All three XQL validation queries return >= 1 row.

test_cases.objective: The encryption stages stitch into one Impact incident.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-EDR-0008` groups the stages from one host into a single critical incident.
Incident severity is Critical and the XSOAR containment playbook is offered.

preventive_controls: Enable Cortex XDR anti-ransomware behavioral protection on Linux hosts to block rapid mass file-rewrite with a uniform new extension.
Keep immutable / off-host backups so recovery-inhibition on the host cannot destroy the only copy.
Restrict write access to data directories and alert on uniform-extension mass renames.
detection_engineering: Alert on a single process modifying many files with one new extension in a short window.
Alert on recurring ransom-note filenames written across directories and on snapshot/backup deletion commands.
Correlate mass-encryption + ransom-note + recovery-inhibition on one host into a single Impact incident.
